name: SSL / HTTPS
description: Checks that the page is served over HTTPS and flags mixed content (http: images, scripts, stylesheets, iframes). HTTPS is a basic trust signal for search and AI platforms, and mixed content can be blocked by browsers or agents.
inputs: rendered DOM: img[src], script[src], link[rel="stylesheet"][href], iframe[src]

scoring.summary: Site check. The scheme is inferred (predicted), since the repo cannot show TLS: host config forcing HTTPS (Strict-Transport-Security header rule, or an http:// -> https:// redirect rule) -> https; else the declared site URL (base URL, else canonical / og:url on pages; localhost ignored) -> http or https, except that an http declaration on a host that serves HTTPS by default (Netlify, Vercel, Cloudflare, GitHub Pages, Firebase) is https; else a known HTTPS host -> https; else unknown. http -> 0. https -> 2, or 1 if any page has mixed content. Unknown -> 1 inconclusive.

rules.condition: inferred scheme is http (declared http:// site URL, nothing forcing HTTPS, host unknown)
no site URL, no canonical/og:url, no HSTS/redirect rule, unknown host
any page matches img[src^="http:"], script[src^="http:"], link[rel="stylesheet"][href^="http:"], iframe[src^="http:"] (case-sensitive prefix, exact rel)
https inferred and no mixed content

rules.note: finding only when the scheme is https by other evidence

scoring.status_mapping: Derived by the engine from the integer score: >= 80% pass, >= 50% warning, else fail; inconclusive results are always a warning.
scoring.inconclusive: When nothing in the repo indicates the production scheme: 1/2 with inconclusive true. Every other result is predicted.

detect.source_procedure: 1) HTTPS evidence: Strict-Transport-Security in host header config for '/', http:// -> https:// rules in _redirects / netlify.toml / vercel.json / firebase.json (forced https). 2) Declared site URL: site.baseUrl (CLI --base-url, home canonical/og:url, sitemap <loc>, CNAME, Hugo baseURL, Astro site), and canonical/og:url on every page (http:// ones become findings). 3) Host defaults from config files (netlify.toml, vercel.json, wrangler.*, firebase.json, CNAME, _headers/_redirects). 4) Mixed content: the four extension selectors over every loaded page, one finding per element. 5) Score: http 0; https 2 (1 with mixed content); unknown 1 inconclusive.
detect.llm_criteria: Model decides the production scheme when config is ambiguous (e.g. no site URL, custom domain on a known host) and whether an http: asset reference is actually rendered on the page (not in comments, docs code blocks or dead components).

parity.note: The protocol is a property of the deployment, not the repo; the plugin infers it from host config, declared URLs and host defaults and marks the result predicted. Mixed content from built HTML matches the extension, but scripts injected at runtime and CMS content are not visible. Protocol-relative (//) and uppercase (HTTP:) URLs are not flagged, as in the extension.

fix_summary: Rewrite http:// asset URLs in templates/content to https:// (auto-fixable when the asset is available over HTTPS) and set the site URL config to https (astro site, Hugo baseURL, Next metadataBase). Enabling HTTPS itself (certificate, forced redirect) is host config and report-only unless the host is file-configured (e.g. netlify.toml redirect, vercel defaults).

divergences.extension: Uses the protocol of the live page URL.
divergences.plugin: Infers the scheme from HSTS / http->https redirect rules, the declared site URL (base URL, canonical, og:url) and host defaults; unknown is 1/2 inconclusive.
divergences.reason: Source vs live: TLS is not visible in the repo.

divergences.extension: Mixed content is checked on the current page only.
divergences.plugin: Site check over every loaded page; any mixed content on any page costs the 0.5 point, one finding per element.
divergences.reason: Site-level audit of all pages; findings group by message across pages.
